input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view: side-by-side parameters and metrics with diff highlighting

## Description

Delivers a run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users select two or more
runs from the runs list and view their parameters and metrics side by side, and
for two selected runs see which parameters and metrics changed (diff
highlighting). This gives data scientists in-platform visibility into what
differs between candidate training and pipeline runs, replacing the exported
spreadsheets described in the strategy's problem statement.

## Scope

- Multi-selection of two or more runs from the existing runs list in the
  Dashboard.
- A comparison view that renders the parameters and metrics of every selected
  run side by side.
- A diff presentation over the same comparison surface: for two selected runs,
  parameters and metrics whose values differ are highlighted.
- Coverage of both run kinds surfaced by the platform today (training runs and
  Data Science Pipelines runs), consumed through the Dashboard's existing
  interfaces to run data — no changes to Data Science Pipelines are in scope.
- Validation that pipeline-run parameters and metrics as served by the
  existing Data Science Pipelines surfaces are complete enough for a
  side-by-side comparison and diff (passive-component validation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the runs list, when a user selects two or more runs and invokes the
  compare action, a comparison view shows each selected run's parameters and
  metrics side by side.
- Given exactly two runs in the comparison view, parameters and metrics whose
  values differ between the two runs are highlighted so the user can see what
  changed.
- The comparison works for both training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs
  as surfaced by the existing runs list, without code changes outside the
  Dashboard; any gap in pipeline-run parameter/metric availability surfaced by
  this validation is reported back to the strategy rather than worked around
  in another component.
- Existing per-run pages (parameters and metrics of a single run) continue to
  function without regression.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- **HLR-3 (P1, consolidated with HLR-1)** — the run "diff" view highlighting
  which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs is a
  presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data, so
  it is delivered by this epic rather than a separate one.

# Link registered model versions to the runs that produced them

## Description

Registered model versions record a reference to the run (training or pipeline)
that produced them, stored and served by the Model Registry. This lineage link
is what lets a comparison be opened starting from a registered model version,
supporting model promotion decisions with traceability back to the producing
experiment.

## Scope

- Define and store a run reference on registered model versions, using the
  Model Registry's existing metadata extension point for structured metadata
  on ModelVersion entities (custom properties) rather than a new schema
  object.
- Expose the run reference through the Model Registry REST API so Dashboard
  surfaces and API consumers can read it.
- Keep the link optional and backward compatible: registration without a run
  reference remains fully supported.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered with knowledge of its producing run, the
  run reference is stored on the model version and retrievable through the
  Model Registry REST API.
- Model versions created without a run reference continue to be created,
  listed, served, and deployed without error, and existing model versions are
  not migrated or altered.
- The run reference round-trips through the documented API surface (written at
  registration, read back unchanged).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1, data side)** — registered model versions link back to the run
  that produced them. The registry-UI entry point that consumes this link is
  tracked separately within the Dashboard component.

# Open a run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

From a registered model version in the Dashboard's Model Registry UI, users
can open the run comparison with the run that produced that model version
pre-selected, and then complete the selection to compare it against other
runs. This connects model promotion decisions to the experiment evidence held
in run parameters and metrics.

## Scope

- An action on a registered model version page in the Model Registry UI (the
  registry section of the Dashboard) that opens the run comparison populated
  with the referenced run.
- Within the opened comparison, the user can add further runs to reach a
  multi-run side-by-side comparison, reusing the comparison view's existing
  selection behavior.
- Graceful handling of model versions that carry no run reference: the action
  is absent or disabled and the page is otherwise unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a run reference, the Model
  Registry UI offers an action that opens the run comparison with that run
  pre-selected.
- Given a registered model version without a run reference, the page renders
  without error and offers no broken path to the comparison.
- From a comparison opened this way, the user can add additional runs and gets
  the same side-by-side parameters/metrics view and two-run diff highlighting
  as when starting from the runs list.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1, UI side)** — "so a comparison can be opened from the Model
  Registry": this epic delivers the registry-UI entry point that consumes the
  run-reference metadata stored on model versions and opens the run
  comparison capability.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

User documentation for the run comparison workflow, covering both entry
points: starting a comparison from the runs list and opening one from a
registered model version in the Model Registry.

## Scope

Content outline (to be authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- Comparing runs from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the
  side-by-side parameters and metrics view, and interpreting the two-run diff
  highlighting of changed parameters and metrics.
- Comparing runs from the Model Registry: opening a comparison from a
  registered model version that links to its producing run, and adding
  further runs to the comparison.
- Prerequisites and limitations as stated by the strategy (comparison is
  within a project; automatic best-run selection and cross-cluster/cross-
  project comparison are out of scope and should not be documented as
  available).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the Model Registry, matching the shipped UI.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  of the run comparison capability and the model-version run linkage before
  publication.
- Documented steps and screenshots reflect the final user-facing flows (no
  references to features that are out of scope).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9015: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs

Strategy status: Refinement Done. Strategy priority: Major. The strategy was not
triaged in Step 0: it spans three components (Dashboard, Model Registry, Data
Science Pipelines) and multiple architecturally distinct work streams (Dashboard
UI, Model Registry backend metadata, documentation authoring), so the
below-threshold path does not apply, and code changes are required, so the
docs-only path does not apply either.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E001 | Run comparison view: side-by-side parameters and metrics with diff highlighting | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E002 | Link registered model versions to the runs that produced them | Implementation | Model Registry | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E003 | Open a run comparison from the Model Registry | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E004 | Document the run comparison workflow | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Docs | P1 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["RHAISTRAT-9015-E001 Run comparison view"] --> E003["RHAISTRAT-9015-E003 Registry entry point"]
    E002["RHAISTRAT-9015-E002 Run linkage on model versions"] --> E003
    E001 --> E004["RHAISTRAT-9015-E004 Documentation"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

Arrows point from dependency to dependent (the epic at the arrow's tail must
complete before the epic at the head starts).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 ∥ E002 (no edge) | Rule 14 | Different components and repos (odh-dashboard vs model-registry), no shared artifacts — the comparison view and the run-reference metadata can be built independently. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (framework/surface → consumer) | The registry entry point's code opens and pre-populates the run comparison view; it builds against that UI surface and cannot be implemented or verified before the comparison view exists. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The registry entry point consumes the run reference stored on registered model versions and served through the Model Registry REST API — an API artifact another epic's code builds against. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation must describe the comparison workflow as built. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation covers the registry-side linkage semantics as built. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation covers the registry entry point to the comparison as built. |

No konflux-onboarding, repo-onboarding, or license-validation epics are needed:
all three affected components are already in the platform and Konflux-onboarded
per architecture context, and no new component is introduced.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001 | Side-by-side comparison of parameters and metrics for two or more selected runs. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | E002, E003 | Split along the component/team boundary: E002 (Model Registry team) stores and serves the run reference on model versions; E003 (RHOAI Dashboard team) adds the registry-UI entry point that opens a comparison. Both halves are needed to satisfy the HLR. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001 (consolidated with HLR-1) | The "diff" view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data — same component, same team, same UI surface. Splitting it out would build the same surface twice and add an artificial serialization edge, so it is covered by the single comparison-view epic at the higher priority (P0). The strategy itself notes the requirements were consolidated from two customer councils with overlapping wording kept. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E004 | Documentation of the comparison workflow from both entry points (runs list and registry). Docs-authoring priority derived from strategy priority Major → P1 per the docs-authoring priority exception. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections.** The strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
   Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, and no
   Non-Functional Requirements; the Affected Components section is a bare list
   without change descriptions or owner teams. Epic ACs were therefore derived
   from the HLRs, and owner teams were inferred from the architecture-context
   "Owning team" fields (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard, Model Registry → Model
   Registry, Data Science Pipelines → RHOAI Pipelines). The docs epic's team
   (RHOAI Docs) is a convention-based inference — Documentation has no
   architecture-context file. Verify team assignments at refinement.
2. **"Training runs" surface assumption (scope trap).** The problem statement
   and HLR-1 speak of "training and pipeline runs", but Training Operator is
   not an affected component and the platform's runs surface is Data Science
   Pipelines. The decomposition assumes training runs are executed (or
   otherwise surfaced) as pipeline runs in the existing runs list. This is
   captured as a verification acceptance criterion on E001 rather than an
   Investigation epic: the strategy's affected-components list implies no
   Training Operator work exists, and the answer does not change which epics
   exist — it would only expand E001's scope. If training runs turn out to
   surface through a different path, re-scope E001 before implementation.
3. **Passive component — Data Science Pipelines.** No code changes are
   expected there: run parameters and metrics are already served through the
   existing KFP v2 surfaces the Dashboard consumes. Validation that
   pipeline-run parameters/metrics are complete enough for side-by-side
   comparison and diff highlighting is folded into E001's acceptance criteria.
4. **No priority inversions detected.** E001 is the only P0 epic and has no
   dependencies; nothing P1/P2 blocks it. HLR-3's P1 label does not push a
   split (see traceability row above).

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — the strategy has no external dependencies with uncertain
timing; all work is in-platform. E001 (P0) delivers standalone user value
(run comparison from the runs list) independent of the registry-linkage work
(E002/E003, P1).

All four HLRs map to epics: HLR-1 (P0) → E001; HLR-2 (P1) → E002 (data side,

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)
No cycles; all edges reference existing epics. Diagram (dependency → dependent)
matches frontmatter exactly: E003 depends on E001+E002; E004 depends on
E001+E002+E003; E001 and E002 are roots. Edges are justified: E001 ∥ E002 per

not a configuration reference); E002 → E003 per Rule 13 (E003's code builds
against the run-reference API field served by the Model Registry REST API — a
build-against API artifact, not a digest/URL config reference); all three
implementation epics → E004 per Rule 11 (docs last). No konflux/repo/license

verification AC on E001 rather than an Investigation — defensible, since the
strategy lists no open questions, Training Operator is not an affected
component, and the answer would only re-scope E001, not change which epics

Component/team tuples are consistent with the architecture-context owning-team
fields (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard, Model Registry → Model Registry) and E004
